gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: It’s a public seafront, so you can bring a pushchair. The beach is shingle and hard going, so I would stick to the promenade or the Western Lawns.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Responsible dog owners are welcome, but it gets crowded and noisy, and the Typhoon is very loud. I would think about how your dog copes before bringing them.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: A picnic is fine, but barbecues and open fires weren’t allowed anywhere on the site in 2026, beaches included. I couldn’t find a clear rule on bringing alcohol, so I would ask the show before you go.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: I couldn’t find a rule on gazebos or windbreaks. Low chairs or cushions work well on the shingle, and I would ask before taking anything big, as space gets tight at the weekend.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: In 2026 there were free water refill points, so bring a reusable bottle. There’s very little shade on the seafront, so keep drinking.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: In 2026 there was a Changing Places toilet at the Bandstand, next to free RADAR toilets. The other public toilets at the Bandstand and the pier cost £1, card only.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: It’s free for everyone, so there’s no carer ticket to sort. If you’re booking paid seating, I would ask about carers when you book.

gtk.title: Hearing support
gtk.text: I couldn’t find anything on hearing loops or BSL. I would contact Visitor Services on 01323 415415 before you go if you need support.

gtk.title: Quiet area
gtk.text: In 2023 and 2024 there was an accessible viewing area for families with profound and multiple learning disabilities, with sunshades and beds. I couldn’t find it confirmed since, so I would ask Visitor Services.

gtk.title: Re-entry
gtk.text: It’s an open public seafront with no gates, so you can pop into town and come back whenever you like.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: In 2026 there were first aid points at the Pier, the Bandstand and the RNLI Museum, and lost persons went to the Lifeguard Station. Pick up a free Kidzsafe wristband and write your mobile number on it.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. Sea mist and low cloud can change the flying, so I would check Airbourne’s social media on the morning.

skipped.flights: I couldn't find any pleasure, helicopter, warbird or balloon flights offered at or from Airbourne. The official FAQ, essential information and where to watch pages don't mention any, and nothing turned up in a wider search.

It may be worth a line, with a link to the Good to know tile: https://www.visiteastbourne.com/airshow/info 2) The same page says there are no cash machines on site (nearest on Terminus Road by The Beacon) and encourages cash, which sits a little awkwardly with the 2026 car parks being card only. The kit list already says bring a card; you may want to add cash for buckets and stalls. 3) The accessibility page for 2027 doesn't mention an accessible viewing area yet; the PMLD area ran in 2023 and 2024: https://www.visiteastbourne.com/airshow/attractions/latest-news/2024/8/21/accessibility-2024-a2844 4) The FAQ already shows 12 to 15 August 2027, which matches the page.
